issues.description: The problem statement gives conflicting guidance about the SealSaloon.stock attribute: one section says the constructor should initialize a final Stock stock (implying an instance field initialized in the constructor), while another section explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static (shared across all instances). This contradiction can confuse students about whether to implement stock as an instance-final field or as a static (final) field and may lead to incorrect implementations that fail tests or deviate from the intended shared-stock design.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the problem statement consistent: explicitly state that the stock attribute must be declared static (e.g. 'private static final Stock stock') in the UML and description, or remove the static requirement if the intended design is instance-scoped. Update the UML to show the static attribute and remove the earlier phrasing that might imply an instance 'final' initialized in the constructor.

issues.description: The UML/problem listing for Stock declares a method emptyStock(): void, but the template Stock class provides clearInventory() (different name) while the solution uses emptyStock(). This method-name/signature mismatch between the problem description and the template will confuse students about which method to implement or call and can break automated tests expecting emptyStock().
issues.suggestedFix: Align method names across artifacts. Either rename template's clearInventory() to emptyStock(), or add a delegating emptyStock() method in the template that calls clearInventory(). Also update the problem statement and UML to use the same method name (preferably emptyStock() to match the UML and solution).

issues.description: The problem statement and solution expect a Stock method named emptyStock(), but the template repository defines this operation as clearInventory(). This naming mismatch for the same conceptual operation (clearing/emptying the stock) can confuse students and cause compilation/test failures because the expected method name differs across artifacts.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method clearInventory() to emptyStock() (or add an emptyStock() wrapper that calls clearInventory()) so the template, problem statement, and solution use the same identifier for clearing the stock.
